The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

The insurer is in appeal challenging the liability fastened on it to pay compensation awarded by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bijapur (henceforth referred as NC: 2023:KHC-K:1344 'the Tribunal'), in MVC No.704/2012, vide judgment and award dated 30.04.2014.
2.
The claim petition discloses that the claimants are the legal heirs of deceased Dasharat Pujari.
It shows that on 24.03.2012, when the deceased was riding his motorcycle, he dashed against a parked tractor and trailer at about 10-30 p.m.
As a result, the deceased suffered injuries and died at the spot.

A claim petition was filed under Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (henceforth referred to as 'MV Act' ), claiming compensation from the owner and insurer of the trailer attached to the tractor.

sentences.text: The owner of the trailer contended that he was not responsible for the accident and therefore, was not liable to indemnify the loss caused due to the death of Dasharat Pujari.
He claimed that he was not the owner of the tractor and trailer as on the date of the accident and therefore, he was not liable to answer the claim made by the claimants.
The insurer of the trailer contested the claim petition contending that the tractor was not insured and what was the insured was only the trailer bearing registration No.MH-13/AJ-3370.
It contended that the tractor was carrying sugar cane on the date of accident and that the deceased riding the motorcycle dashed against the trailer resulting in accident.
Therefore, it contended that it was not liable to pay any compensation as the tractor itself was not insured.

Further, it contended that the tractor was attached to trailer and loaded with sugar cane and that the deceased was trapped in the rear of the trailer, indicating that he was speeding and was negligent.
It contended that the negligence, if any, is only on the part of the deceased and since the tractor itself was not insured, it was not liable to indemnify the owner of the trailer.
Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
Claimant No.1 was examined as P.W.1 and she marked Exs.P.1 to P.6.

The insurer examined one of its officials as R.W.1 and marked Exs.R.1 to R.4.
6.

Based on oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the accident was due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the tractor, who had carelessly parked the tractor in the middle of the road and since the accident occurred at 10-30 p.m., it held that the driver of the tractor was negligent and was responsible for the accident.
Even otherwise, it held that the petition was filed under Section 163-A of the MV Act, 1988, question of proving negligence on the part of the driver of the tractor did not arise.

The Tribunal considered the income of the deceased at a sum of Rs.36,000/- per annum and deducted 1/3rd towards his personal and living expenses and applied maximum multiplier at 18 and awarded compensation of Rs.4,32,000/- towards loss of dependency,
Rs.4,000/- towards funeral expenses, Rs.5,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.7,500/-
NC: 2023:KHC-K:1344 towards love and affection.
It directed the insurer of the trailer to pay the compensation along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till its realization.
Being aggrieved by the liability cast upon the insurer, the present appeal is filed.
7. Learned counsel for the insurer contended that the trailer alone was insured and not the tractor and therefore, the insurer was exempt from the liability to pay compensation.
She contended that Section 2(28) read with Section 146 of the MV Act, 1988 makes it compulsory that tractor and trailer should be insured.

She relied upon a judgment of the Division Bench of this Court in the case of The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. D. Laxman and Ors.1 and contended that both the vehicles need to be insured to sustain a claim for compensation either under Section 166 of the MV Act, 1988 or under Section 163-A of the MV Act, 1988.

sentences.text: Therefore, she contends that unless the tractor and trailer were insured, there could be no claim for compensation only against the insurer of the trailer.

8. Per contra, learned counsel for the claimants contended that the accident occurred when the vehicle was parked on the middle of the road and therefore, question whether the tractor was insured or not is purely academic.
He submitted that the accident happened on 10-30 p.m., when the tractor with two trailers were parked on the road and therefore, the claim petition against the insurer of the trailer is maintainable.
I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the claimants as well as the learned counsel for the insurer.

10. It is no doubt true that perusal of Section 2(28) read with Section 146 of MV Act, 1988, makes it mandatory that all vehicles/motor vehicles which are brought for use on public road have to be compulsorily insured against risk to third parties.

In the instant case, trailers attached to the tractor were loaded with sugar cane were parked in the center of the road at 10.30 p.m. without switching on hazard light or signal to the other users of the road.
If the lights were on, the deceased would not have dashed against the rear trailer.

Therefore, a claim petition under Section 163-A of the MV Act,
1988 is maintainable.
The Tribunal has appreciated this question and has rightly held that the claim petition was maintainable against the insurer of the trailer without proceeding against the insurer of the tractor.

Since the owner of the tractor has failed to get the same insured and NC:
2023:KHC-K:1344 has contributed to the accident, the insurer may proceed against the owner of the tractor to recover the compensation paid to the claimants.
In that view of the matter, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal did not warrant interference.
In view of the above, the appeal lacks merit and is dismissed.
Any amount in deposit is ordered to be transferred to the Tribunal for necessary orders.
It is made clear that the insurer is at liberty to take out separate proceedings to recover the money paid by it to the claimants in this proceedings.
